title: windowed-attention-preemptive-fusion-and-scheduler-optimization
author: Leila Martinez
release_notes: Introduces a new windowed attention fusion path and a preemptive scheduler which reduces p95 latency and improves throughput for mixed short/long request workloads. No user-facing API changes. Recommend rolling to Dedicated nodes in canary before wide deployment.
description:
Summary: Add a windowed attention fusion kernel and a preemptive scheduling policy that cooperates with the KV cache warmup heuristic and continuous batching engine. This PR targets mixed workloads where short interactive requests are frequently interleaved with long-compute generations. The goal is to reduce tail latency for latency-sensitive traffic while preserving throughput for long sequences.

Motivation: We observe that existing continuous-batching + fused FlashAttention paths favor throughput and can starve short requests at the scheduler boundary, and the KV cache warmup causes large cold-start penalties when long sequences evict warm prefix state. This change introduces a windowed fusion kernel that fuses QK/V ops for small and medium sequence windows and exposes a preemptive scheduling hint that allows short requests to bypass global batching in favor of bounded micro-batches.

Design:
- New kernel: src/runtime/attn/windowed_fuse_kernel.cu provides fused QK/QV compute for windows up to 1024 tokens with special-case rotary/rope handling to avoid rematerializing offsets for every token. The kernel uses a two-stage warp strategy: small-window in-warp accumulation and large-window multi-warp staging to keep SM occupancy high.
- Scheduler: src/runtime/scheduler/preemptive_scheduler.cpp implements a preemptive path in the continuous batcher. It tracks estimated remaining-token counts and will preempt long-standing micro-batches when short requests fall below a latency-target threshold. Preemption is cooperative: running kernels are allowed to finish their current-toy-op and the long batch is split and requeued to a dedicated throughput lane.
- KV cache warmup: src/runtime/kv/cache_warmup.cpp adds an adaptive warmup that keeps frequently-used prefix shards in a small hotset and biases eviction away from them during short-request preemption.
- Runtime hooks: Integrates with the routing layer (src/runtime/routing/policy.cc) to annotate requests with latency targets and with the continuous batching controller (src/runtime/batcher/controller.cc) to expose a fast-path for preempted micro-batches.
- Fallbacks: On devices that do not support required SM capabilities, the scheduler falls back to existing FlashAttention kernels. The new kernel is registered behind a capability check and model-profile thresholds.

Implementation notes and trade-offs:
- The fused rotary/rope handling avoids a global remap by keeping per-window offset remapping in shared memory; this increases shared memory use but reduces global memory traffic for common prefix patterns.
- Preemption adds scheduling jitter; to mitigate that we implemented token-estimate smoothing and a maximum preemption rate.
- We added instrumentation counters for preemption events, warmset hits, and kernel selection decisions.

Performance results (lab, rtx-a100 cluster, mixed workload):
- Short-only (len 64): p50 ~0.9x baseline (slight overhead), p95 -18% latency.
- Mixed (80% short len64 + 20% long len2048): overall throughput +18%, short p95 -28%, long throughput -3% (isolated long throughput unchanged).
- Cold KV start: cold-start latency reduced by ~30% on average due to hotset warmup.

Testing and CI:
- Unit tests added for kernel correctness including rotary/rope edgecases.
- Scheduler tests simulate mixed traffic and verify preemption invariants and backlog fairness.
- Microbenchmarks added to bench harness; presubmit bench run included in ci/bench-presubmit.yml. CI had a flaky test on A100 multi-GPU in first run; re-run passed.

Review conversation snapshot:
- Samir (review): "Great design. Two asks: add a metric for number of preemptions per-minute at the tenant level; and document the cost/benefit tradeoffs in the rollout doc."
- Author (Leila): "Added tenant-level preemption counter and expanded rollout doc with a canary playbook and knob recommendations."
- Morgan (review): "Can you ensure fallback path preserves exact fp16 accumulation behavior (we saw a small delta in a model smoke-test)?"
- Author: "Fixed accumulation path in kernel and added fp16 equivalence tests. Numbers now match within tolerance."
- Diego (review): "Consider a switch to make preemption opt-in per-route for enterprise customers; we should avoid surprising perf shifts."
- Author: "Added per-route preemption flag with default enabled and documented in routing API. Ops can disable for Dedicated pools during rollouts."

Merge and rollout:
- Merged via squash on 2026-03-02 after green CI and +2 approvals.
- Rollout plan in docs/perf/windowed-fusion.md: start with 5% canary on Dedicated pool nodes, monitor preemption counters and p95 latency for interactive routes, then progressive ramp to 25/50/100%.

Ops knobs: preemption_enabled (global), per_route_preemption (route config), kernel_selection_thresholds.

Backward compatibility and risk:
- No API surface changes.
- Kernel uses more shared memory; may reduce concurrency on small GPU types. Recommended to gate on profile detection to avoid regression on constrained SKUs.

Observability additions:
- New metrics: scheduler.preemptions.count, kv.hotset.hit_ratio, kernel.selection.path.
- Tracing: span annotations for preemption decisions and kernel selection.

Related work and references:
- ENG-2741 (project planning), ENG-2838 (kv warmup follow-up), previous flashfusion and rotary optimizations in kernel library.

Notes for reviewers: check arithmetic correctness in windowed_fuse_kernel.cu (rotary offset math is subtle), verify microbenchmark harness on multi-GPU CI to reduce flakiness.
